items.title: Two recorded searches returned no records
items.whyItMatters: Nothing was retrieved or appraised, so no effect size or certainty can be borrowed from elsewhere.
items.opportunity: Answer the question from the line's own logs and report the empty searches in the methods.

items.title: Message-level timestamps are not yet accessible
items.whyItMatters: Without the vendor agreement neither the pre-implementation series nor fidelity measures can be built.
items.opportunity: Keep the data-sharing agreement as a gate on the analysis and record the date it is signed.

items.title: No concurrent comparison group
items.whyItMatters: The protocol goes live for everyone, so a change in waits could reflect demand or season.
items.opportunity: Use an interrupted time series with a year of weekly data before go-live and adjust for season and demand.

items.title: The keyword flag may miss risk expressed indirectly or in other languages
items.whyItMatters: Texters who describe risk without the listed words, or in a language other than English, would not move up the queue.
items.opportunity: Report flag rates by conversation language and review a de-identified sample of unflagged escalations with the agency's clinical lead.

items.title: Abandoned conversations hide who gave up
items.whyItMatters: Texters who leave the queue may be those at greatest risk.
items.opportunity: Measure abandonment by hour and by whether the texter returned within 24 hours.

errorsFound: The need hopes to compare before and after; with the protocol live for everyone this is an interrupted time series, not a two-group comparison.
reevaluation: The gaps point to an implementation study built on the line's own logs, with RE-AIM delivery and acceptance outcomes and a time series of waits, and with the data agreement as the gate on any analysis.
summary: Five gaps: empty searches, inaccessible timestamps, no comparison group, flag equity and hidden abandonment.
